source.title: Merrill’s Atlas — supplied PDF
source.pageNumbering: PDF page numbers, starting at 1; not printed textbook pages.
source.note: Concise study summaries of the supplied text. IR sizes reflect its CR-plate recommendations; digital receptor selection follows department protocol.

commonEvaluation: Side marker within the collimated field, clear of anatomy of interest.
Sharp bony trabecular detail and surrounding soft tissue; no motion.
symbols: ⟂ perpendicular · ∥ parallel · CR central ray · IR image receptor · SID source-to-image distance

views.name: PA
key: PIP centering; entire digit and distal metacarpal.
position: Seated; palm down.
Extend and separate digits; affected digit centered.
collimation: 1 in beyond digit; include distal metacarpal, 1 in proximal to MCP.
evaluation: Equal shaft concavity and soft tissue on both sides.
Open IP/MCP joints; no adjacent-digit overlap.

views.name: Lateral
key: Digits 2–3: radial side down. Digits 4–5: ulnar side down.
position: Extend affected digit; flex others away.
Support digits 3–4 ∥ IR; adjust to true lateral.
collimation: 1 in beyond digit; include distal metacarpal, 1 in proximal to MCP.
evaluation: Nail in profile; concave anterior phalangeal surfaces.
Open IP joints; proximal phalanx/MCP clear of adjacent digits.

views.name: PA Oblique
key: 45° lateral rotation; digit ∥ IR opens joints.
position: Palm down; rotate laterally 45° onto support.
Extend and separate digits.
collimation: 1 in beyond digit; include distal metacarpal, 1 in proximal to MCP.
evaluation: Open IP/MCP joints; no adjacent-digit overlap.

views.name: AP
key: Posterior thumb against IR; avoid obliquity.
position: Seated; internally rotate arm and hand.
Hold other digits back; thumb extended ∥ IR.
collimation: 1 in beyond thumb; include trapezium and 1 in proximal to CMC.
evaluation: Open IP/MCP joints; first metacarpal included.

views.name: PA
key: Elevated thumb produces more magnification than AP.
position: Hand on ulnar side; abduct thumb.
Support thumb with dorsal surface ∥ IR.
collimation: 1 in beyond thumb; include trapezium and 1 in proximal to CMC.

views.name: Lateral
key: Natural hand arch positions thumb laterally.
position: Palm down; fingers flexed or supported.
Adjust hand arch until thumb is truly lateral.
collimation: 1 in beyond thumb; include trapezium and 1 in proximal to CMC.
evaluation: Thumbnail in profile; anterior shaft concavity.

views.name: PA Oblique
key: Palm flat naturally obliques the abducted thumb.
position: Palm against IR; thumb abducted.
Slight ulnar deviation; thumb aligned with IR.
collimation: 1 in beyond thumb; include trapezium and 1 in proximal to CMC.
evaluation: Concavity on elevated side of proximal phalanx/metacarpal.

views.name: Robert
key: ⟂ CR enters CMC. See modifications for an obscured joint.
position: Shoulder, elbow and wrist in one plane.
Internally rotate arm; thumbnail down.
Hyperextend hand to clear palm; thumb not oblique.
collimation: 1 in beyond thumb, including 1 in proximal to CMC.
purpose: First CMC alignment, arthritis and Bennett fracture.

views.name: Long and Rafert
key: 15° proximal; enters CMC, not MCP.
position: Shoulder, elbow and wrist in one plane.
Internally rotate arm; thumbnail down.
Hyperextend hand to clear palm; thumb not oblique.
collimation: 1 in beyond thumb, including 1 in proximal to CMC.
purpose: Open CMC and displace overlying palm.

views.name: Lewis
key: 10–15° proximal; enters MCP, not CMC.
position: Shoulder, elbow and wrist in one plane.
Internally rotate arm; thumbnail down.
Hyperextend hand to clear palm; thumb not oblique.
collimation: 1 in beyond thumb, including 1 in proximal to CMC.
purpose: Open CMC and displace overlying palm.

views.name: Burman
key: 45° toward elbow; magnified CMC.
position: Seated; hyperextend wrist.
Rotate hand internally; abduct thumb flat on IR.
collimation: Center tightly on first CMC and adjacent bone.
precautions: Only when wrist hyperextension is not contraindicated.

views.name: Folio
key: Patient-controlled bilateral thumb stress for UCL injury.
position: Hands on ulnar borders; thumbnails ∥ IR.
Tape roll between first metacarpals; band around distal thumbs.
Patient pulls thumbs apart for exposure.
collimation: Third metacarpals laterally; thumb bases proximally; 1 in beyond thumbnails.
purpose: Compare first MCP joints/angles for skier’s thumb.
evaluation: First metacarpals and MCP joints; band/tape correctly placed.

views.name: PA
key: Third MCP centering.
position: Seated; forearm on table.
Palm flat; fingers extended and slightly separated.
collimation: 1 in beyond hand, including 1 in proximal to ulnar styloid.

views.name: PA Oblique
key: 45° lateral rotation; support digits ∥ IR for open IP joints.
position: Palm down; rotate laterally 45°.
Extend digits on wedge; thumb separated.
collimation: 1 in beyond hand, including 1 in proximal to ulnar styloid.
evaluation: Open MCP joints; IP joints open when supported.

views.name: Lateral Mediolateral
key: Radial side against IR.
position: Radial side down; palm ⟂ IR.
Extend digits; thumb at right angle to palm.
collimation: 1 in beyond hand, including 1 in proximal to ulnar styloid.
evaluation: Phalanges, metacarpals and distal radius/ulna superimposed.

views.name: Lateral Lateromedial
key: Ulnar side against IR.
position: Ulnar side down; palm ⟂ IR.
Extend digits; thumb at right angle to palm.
collimation: 1 in beyond hand, including 1 in proximal to ulnar styloid.
evaluation: Phalanges, metacarpals and distal radius/ulna superimposed.

views.name: Fan Lateral
key: Phalanges separated; metacarpals stay superimposed.
position: Ulnar side down; palm ⟂ IR.
Fan fingers on wedge; thumb abducted and supported.

notes: Source discrepancy: the same section lists fifth MCP for lateromedial hand; Fig. 5.61 depicts second MCP centering for fan lateral.

collimation: 1 in beyond hand, including 1 in proximal to ulnar styloid.
evaluation: Individual phalanges visible except proximal bases.

views.name: Lateral in Flexion
key: Natural finger flexion when extension is limited.
position: Ulnar side down; relax fingers into natural arch.
Superimpose digits; thumb ∥ IR.
collimation: 1 in beyond hand, including 1 in proximal to ulnar styloid.

views.name: Norgaard
key: Bilateral 45° half-supination; ball-catcher variant.
position: Both hands half-supinated on 45° supports.
Fingers extended or cupped; thumbs abducted.
collimation: 1 in beyond hand, including 1 in proximal to ulnar styloid.
purpose: Early rheumatoid changes; fifth-metacarpal base fracture.
evaluation: Both hands from carpals to fingertips.
Metacarpal heads/proximal phalangeal bases clear of overlap.

views.name: PA
key: Flex digits slightly to bring carpals against IR.
position: Shoulder, elbow and wrist level.
Palm down; forearm aligned; slightly arch MCPs.
collimation: 2.5 in proximal/distal to wrist; 1 in beyond sides.
evaluation: No rotation; open distal radioulnar space.
No excessive finger flexion obscuring metacarpals.

views.name: AP
key: Carpal interspaces better demonstrated than PA.
position: Supinate hand/forearm.
Support digits to bring wrist against IR.
collimation: 2.5 in proximal/distal to wrist; 1 in beyond sides.
evaluation: Carpals, distal radius/ulna and proximal metacarpals.
No rotation or digit overlap over metacarpals.

views.name: Lateral
key: Superimpose distal radius and ulna.
position: Elbow 90°; shoulder/elbow/wrist level.
Ulnar side down; epicondyles and styloids ⟂ IR.
collimation: 2.5 in proximal/distal to wrist; 1 in beyond sides.

views.name: PA Oblique Lateral Rotation
key: Radial carpals: trapezium and distal scaphoid.
position: From palm down, rotate laterally 45°.
Support wrist; slightly extend; ulnar-deviate for scaphoid.

cr.target: Midcarpal area, just distal to radius

collimation: 2.5 in proximal/distal to wrist; 1 in beyond sides.

views.name: AP Oblique Medial Rotation
key: Merrill’s labels this AP, not PA. Pisiform in profile.
position: Supinated forearm; rotate wrist medially 45°.
collimation: 2.5 in proximal/distal to wrist; 1 in beyond sides.
evaluation: Pisiform, triquetrum and hamate hook in profile, free of overlap.

views.name: Ulnar Deviation
key: Reduces scaphoid foreshortening.
position: PA wrist; elbow 90°.
Keep forearm still; deviate hand toward ulna.

notes: Source allows 10–15° proximal/distal CR adjustment for delineation.

collimation: 2.5 in proximal/distal to wrist; 1 in beyond sides.
evaluation: No wrist rotation; maximum tolerated ulnar deviation.

views.name: Radial Deviation
key: Opens medial-side carpal interspaces.
position: PA wrist; keep forearm still.
Deviate hand toward radius.
collimation: 2.5 in proximal/distal to wrist; 1 in beyond sides.
evaluation: Maximum radial deviation; medial interspaces demonstrated.

views.name: Stecher
key: 20° elevated IR OR 20° CR toward elbow.
position: PA wrist; finger end of IR elevated 20°.

notes: Alternative: flat IR/wrist; CR 20° toward elbow.
Clenched-fist variant uses PA wrist and no CR angle.

collimation: 2.5 in proximal/distal to wrist; 1 in beyond sides.

views.name: Gaynor-Hart Inferosuperior
key: 25–30° to hand axis; carpal canal tangential.
position: Hyperextend wrist; hand as vertical as possible.
Slight radial rotation separates pisiform/hamate.

cr.target: Palm, 1 in distal to third-metacarpal base

collimation: 1 in beyond three sides of wrist shadow.
purpose: Carpal canal; hook of hamate and pisiform.
evaluation: Pisiform in profile, clear of overlap; hamate hook visible.
precautions: Do not force a painful wrist into hyperextension.

views.name: Gaynor-Hart Superoinferior
key: Lean forward to make carpal canal tangent to beam.
position: Dorsiflex wrist as tolerated; lean forward.
45° palmar wedge may assist limited dorsiflexion.
collimation: Palmar wrist and proximal third of metacarpals; 1 in beyond sides.
evaluation: Carpal arch; pisiform clear in profile.

views.name: AP
key: Supinate hand; include both joints.
position: Seated; entire arm in one plane.
Elbow extended; epicondyles ∥ IR.
collimation: 2 in beyond wrist/elbow; 1 in beyond sides.
evaluation: Radial head/neck slightly overlap ulna; epicondyles not distorted.

views.name: Lateral
key: 90° elbow; thumb up; both joints included.
position: Seated; humerus/forearm level.
Ulnar side down; epicondyles/styloids ⟂ IR.
collimation: 2 in beyond wrist/elbow; 1 in beyond sides.
evaluation: Radial head over coronoid; radial tuberosity anterior.

views.name: AP
key: Open humeroradial joint.
position: Shoulder/elbow/wrist level; extend elbow.
Supinate; epicondyles ∥ IR.
collimation: 3 in proximal/distal to elbow; 1 in beyond sides.
evaluation: Slight radial head/neck overlap over ulna.
No epicondylar rotation; humeroradial joint open.

views.name: Lateral
key: 90° flexion; olecranon in profile.
position: Elbow 90°; upper arm/forearm level.
Thumb up; epicondyles ⟂ IR.
collimation: 3 in proximal/distal to elbow; 1 in beyond sides.
evaluation: Radial tuberosity anterior; radial head partly over coronoid.

views.name: AP Oblique Medial Rotation
key: Coronoid process in profile.
position: Extend arm; rotate entire extremity medially 45°.
collimation: 3 in proximal/distal to elbow; 1 in beyond sides.
evaluation: Radial head/neck overlap ulna; olecranon in fossa.

views.name: AP Oblique Lateral Rotation
key: Radial head/neck free of ulna.
position: Extend arm; rotate laterally 45°.
collimation: 3 in proximal/distal to elbow; 1 in beyond sides.
purpose: Radial head, neck, tuberosity and capitulum.

views.name: AP Partial Flexion Distal Humerus
key: Humerus ∥ IR; proximal forearm is foreshortened.
position: Keep humerus flat; support raised forearm.
Supinate if possible.

notes: Distal CR angulation may be needed into the joint, depending on flexion.

collimation: 3 in proximal/distal to elbow; 1 in beyond sides.
purpose: Distal humerus when extension is limited.
evaluation: Distal humerus undistorted; closed elbow joint.

views.name: AP Partial Flexion Proximal Forearm
key: Forearm ∥ IR; distal humerus is foreshortened.
position: Raise seated patient until dorsal forearm rests flat.
Supinate hand.
collimation: 3 in proximal/distal to elbow; 1 in beyond sides.
purpose: Proximal forearm when extension is limited.
evaluation: Partly open joint; foreshortened distal humerus.

views.name: Coyle 90°
key: 90° elbow + CR toward shoulder → radial head.
position: Seated, joints level; hand pronated.
Flex elbow 90°; support wrist as needed.
collimation: 3 in proximal/distal to elbow; 1 in beyond sides.
purpose: Radial head without full elbow extension.
evaluation: Radial head/neck/tuberosity mostly free of ulna; tuberosity posterior.

views.name: Coyle 80°
key: 80° elbow + CR away from shoulder → coronoid.
position: Seated, joints level; hand pronated.
Flex elbow 80°.
collimation: 3 in proximal/distal to elbow; 1 in beyond sides.
evaluation: Elongated coronoid in profile; radial head/neck overlap ulna.

views.name: AP Upright
key: Epicondyles ∥ IR; greater tubercle in profile.
position: Upright; slight arm abduction; supinate.
Epicondyles ∥ IR.
collimation: Include shoulder/elbow; 2 in beyond joints, 1 in beyond sides.
precautions: Do not rotate or abduct a suspected fracture.

views.name: Lateral Upright
key: Epicondyles superimposed; lesser tubercle medial in profile.
position: Upright; internally rotate arm; elbow about 90°.
Hand on hip; epicondyles ⟂ IR.
collimation: Include shoulder/elbow; 2 in beyond joints, 1 in beyond sides.
evaluation: Epicondyles superimposed; greater tubercle over head.
precautions: Do not rotate or abduct a suspected fracture.

views.name: AP Recumbent
key: Epicondyles ∥ IR; greater tubercle in profile.
position: Supine; elevate opposite shoulder or support arm/IR.
Extend elbow; supinate; epicondyles ∥ IR.
collimation: Include shoulder/elbow; 2 in beyond joints, 1 in beyond sides.
precautions: Do not rotate or abduct a suspected fracture.

views.name: Lateral Recumbent
key: Epicondyles superimposed; lesser tubercle medial in profile.
position: Supine; abduct arm; rotate forearm medially.
Back of hand against side; epicondyles ⟂ IR.
collimation: Include shoulder/elbow; 2 in beyond joints, 1 in beyond sides.
evaluation: Epicondyles superimposed; greater tubercle over head.
precautions: Do not rotate or abduct a suspected fracture.

views.name: Trauma Lateral
key: Horizontal beam; this method emphasizes distal humerus.
position: Recumbent/lateral recumbent; IR near axilla.
Support humerus; flex elbow only if permitted.
collimation: 2 in distal to elbow; 1 in beyond sides; upper edge within IR.
purpose: Distal humerus without forced arm rotation.
precautions: Do not force injured arm movement.

views.name: AP External Rotation
key: Greater tubercle lateral in profile.
position: Upright or supine; thorax ∥ IR.
Supinate; slightly abduct arm; epicondyles ∥ IR.
ir: 10 × 12 in; grid. Crosswise: clavicle; lengthwise: more humerus.
collimation: Include superior scapula, proximal humerus and clavicle.
precautions: Do not rotate arm for suspected fracture/dislocation.

views.name: AP Neutral Rotation
key: Greater tubercle partly overlaps humeral head.
position: Upright or supine; thorax ∥ IR.
Palm against thigh; epicondyles about 45° to IR.
ir: 10 × 12 in; grid. Crosswise: clavicle; lengthwise: more humerus.
collimation: Include superior scapula, proximal humerus and clavicle.
evaluation: Head in partial profile; greater tubercle partly superimposed.
precautions: Do not rotate arm for suspected fracture/dislocation.

views.name: AP Internal Rotation
key: Lesser tubercle medial in profile.
position: Upright or supine; thorax ∥ IR.
Back of hand on hip; epicondyles ⟂ IR.
ir: 10 × 12 in; grid. Crosswise: clavicle; lengthwise: more humerus.
collimation: Include superior scapula, proximal humerus and clavicle.
precautions: Do not rotate arm for suspected fracture/dislocation.

views.name: Grashey
key: Open glenohumeral joint; scapula ∥ IR.
position: Posterior oblique toward affected side, usually 35–45°.
Slight arm abduction; palm on abdomen.

cr.target: 2 in medial and 2 in inferior to superolateral shoulder
notes: Recumbent positioning may need up to 60° body rotation.

ir: 10 × 12 in; grid. Crosswise: clavicle; lengthwise: more humerus.
collimation: Include superior scapula, proximal humerus and clavicle.

views.name: Lawrence — Transthoracic Lateral
key: Trauma option: do not move injured arm.
position: Affected side against IR.
Raise unaffected arm/shoulder; injured arm stays still.

notes: 10–15° cephalad if unaffected shoulder cannot be raised.

ir: 10 × 12 in; grid. Crosswise: clavicle; lengthwise: more humerus.
collimation: Include superior scapula, proximal humerus and clavicle.
evaluation: Scapula over thoracic spine; proximal humerus visible through lung.
views.respiration: Full inspiration; source also permits slow breathing with long exposure.

views.name: Lawrence — Inferosuperior Axial
key: Separate Lawrence method: beam through axilla.
position: Supine; elevate shoulder about 3 in.
Abduct arm toward 90° (minimum 20°); external rotation.
IR against superior shoulder; head turned away.

notes: Medial CR angle increases with abduction.

ir: 10 × 12 in; grid. Crosswise: clavicle; lengthwise: more humerus.
collimation: Include superior scapula, proximal humerus and clavicle.
evaluation: Coracoid anterior; AC joint projected through humeral head.
precautions: Do not force abduction in an injured shoulder.

views.name: Scapular Y
key: Head normally centered over Y; dislocation assessment.
position: Anterior oblique 45–60°; scapula ⟂ IR.
Arm position does not change head–glenoid relationship.
ir: 10 × 12 in; grid. Crosswise: clavicle; lengthwise: more humerus.
collimation: Include superior scapula, proximal humerus and clavicle.
evaluation: Scapular borders superimposed; body clear of ribs.
Normal head/glenoid overlap at Y junction.

views.name: Pearson
key: Upright; weights attached to wrists, not held.
position: Arms unsupported; shoulders level; no rotation.
Bilateral images without, then with equal 5–10 lb wrist weights.

cr.target: Midline at AC level; individual AC joint if separate

collimation: 6 × 17 in bilateral; 6 × 8 in per side if separate.
evaluation: Both AC joints included; no leaning.
Separation, if present, demonstrated with weights.

views.name: AP
key: Lateral half above scapula; medial half over thorax.
position: Supine or upright; shoulders level.
Arms at sides; clavicle centered.
collimation: 8 × 12 in; include entire clavicle and both joints.
evaluation: Lateral half above scapula; medial half overlaps thorax.

views.name: AP Axial
key: 15–30° cephalad lifts clavicle above ribs.
position: Upright/supine; clavicle centered.
Lordotic alternative if tolerated.

notes: Lordotic alternative: 0–15° cephalad; thinner chest needs greater angle.

collimation: 8 × 12 in; include entire clavicle and both joints.
evaluation: Both joints included; clavicle more horizontal.

views.name: PA
key: Clavicle nearer IR reduces magnification.
position: Prone or standing facing IR; no rotation.
collimation: 8 × 12 in; include entire clavicle and both joints.
evaluation: Entire clavicle; lateral half above scapula.

views.name: PA Axial
key: 15–30° caudad; reverse of AP axial.
position: Prone or standing facing IR.
collimation: 8 × 12 in; include entire clavicle and both joints.
views.respiration: As AP axial: suspend after full inspiration.

views.name: AP
key: Abduct arm 90° to draw scapula laterally.
position: Upright/supine; body not rotated toward affected side.
Arm abducted 90°; elbow flexed.

cr.target: Midscapula, about 2 in inferior to coracoid

collimation: Include acromion through inferior angle.
evaluation: Scapula not slanted; acromion/inferior angle included.
views.respiration: Slow breathing to blur lung detail.

views.name: Lateral
key: Arm placement clears the specific area of interest.
position: Anterior oblique 45–60°; scapula ⟂ IR.
Body: arm up/on head or across chest.
Processes: back of hand on posterior thorax.
collimation: Include acromion through inferior angle.
evaluation: Scapular body clear of ribs; humerus clear of target.

views.name: AP Oblique
key: Rotate away from affected side to clear rib cage.
position: Posterior oblique 15–25°; arm up or across chest.
Steeper alternative: 25–35°, elbow on forehead.
collimation: Include acromion through inferior angle.
purpose: Oblique scapula, nearly free of ribs.
evaluation: Lateral scapular border adjacent to ribs.

views.name: AP
key: ⟂ CR; IP joints less well demonstrated than axial.
position: Supine/seated; knee flexed; sole on IR.
Toes separated; foot aligned.
collimation: 1 in beyond toes; include 1 in proximal to MTP joints.
evaluation: Entire toes and distal metatarsals included.

views.name: AP Axial
key: 15° toward heel opens IP/MTP spaces.
position: Supine/seated; sole on IR; toes separated.

notes: Alternative: elevate foot on 15° wedge with ⟂ beam.

collimation: 1 in beyond toes; include 1 in proximal to MTP joints.

views.name: PA
key: Prone; dorsal toes on IR.
position: Prone; support foot so toes lie horizontally.
Center third MTP.
collimation: 1 in beyond toes; include 1 in proximal to MTP joints.
evaluation: Symmetric shafts; no overlap between toes.

views.name: AP Oblique
key: 30–45° rotation. First MTP may remain closed.
position: Supine/seated; rotate foot medially 30–45°.
For individual toes: lateral oblique may suit toes 4–5.
collimation: 1 in beyond toes; include 1 in proximal to MTP joints.
evaluation: Open IP and MTP 2–5 spaces; separated toes.

views.name: Lateral
key: Great toe: IP centering. Lesser toes: PIP.
position: Toes 1–2: medial foot against IR.
Toes 3–5: lateral foot against IR.
Move other toes away; affected toe truly lateral.

cr.target: Great-toe IP or lesser-toe PIP joint

collimation: 1 in beyond toes; include 1 in proximal to MTP joints.
evaluation: Nail in profile; plantar phalangeal concavity.
Open IP joints; proximal phalanx clear of adjacent toes.
precautions: Manipulate toes only if no deformity is apparent.

views.name: Tangential Lewis
key: Prone; dorsiflex great toe.
position: Prone; ankle supported.
Great toe against table; ball of foot ⟂ tabletop.
collimation: 3 × 3 in at first MTP.

views.name: Tangential Holly
key: Seated; plantar surface 75° to IR.
position: Seated; medial foot border vertical.
Hold toes back with gauze; plantar surface 75° to IR.
collimation: 3 × 3 in at first MTP.

views.name: AP
key: ⟂ CR; less-open TMT spaces than axial.
position: Supine/seated; knee flexed; sole flat.
No foot rotation.
collimation: 1 in beyond foot, toes and heel.
evaluation: Bases 2–5 overlap; toes through tarsals included.

views.name: AP Axial
key: 10° toward heel → beam ⟂ metatarsals.
position: Supine/seated; sole flat; foot straight.
collimation: 1 in beyond foot, toes and heel.
evaluation: Open medial–intermediate cuneiform joint; no rotation.

views.name: AP Oblique Medial Rotation
key: 30° medial; cuboid and lateral joints.
position: Supine/seated; knee flexed.
Rotate whole leg medially; plantar surface 30° to IR.
collimation: 1 in beyond foot, toes and heel.
purpose: Cuboid, sinus tarsi and lateral intertarsal/TMT joints.

views.name: AP Oblique Lateral Rotation
key: 30° lateral; first/second metatarsal bases.
position: Supine; knee flexed.
Rotate laterally 30°; support elevated side.
collimation: 1 in beyond foot, toes and heel.
evaluation: Minimal medial/intermediate cuneiform overlap; navicular less foreshortened.

views.name: Lateral
key: Mediolateral: lateral foot against IR.
position: Affected side down; support knee.
Foot 90° to leg; plantar forefoot ⟂ IR.
collimation: 1 in beyond foot; include medial malleolus.
evaluation: Fibula over posterior tibia; tibiotalar joint shown.

views.name: Weight-Bearing Lateral Longitudinal Arch
key: Lateromedial, standing; evaluates longitudinal arch.
position: Stand with equal weight on both feet.
Vertical IR against medial foot; support for balance.
collimation: 1 in beyond foot and above medial malleolus.
evaluation: Entire foot/distal leg; metatarsal heads superimposed.

views.name: Weight-Bearing AP Axial
key: Both feet, equally loaded; 48 in SID.
position: Stand on protected IR; feet centered side by side.
Weight equal; right/left and upright markers.

cr.angle: 10° toward heels; ≥15° often needed for clearance

collimation: 1 in beyond foot, toes and heel.
evaluation: Both feet centered; toes through tarsals included.

views.name: Weight-Bearing AP Axial Composite
key: Two exposures; affected foot stays still.
position: Standing; IR under affected foot.
Opposite foot behind for forefoot; ahead for hindfoot.

cr.target: First: third-metatarsal base. Second: posterior ankle; exits plantar surface at lateral-malleolus level.

collimation: 1 in beyond foot, toes and heel.
purpose: Full loaded foot outline, clear of leg.
evaluation: Entire foot; forefoot/hindfoot shown without leg overlap.

views.name: Axial Plantodorsal
key: 40° cephalad to foot axis; sustentaculum medial in profile.
position: Supine/seated; leg extended.
Dorsiflex foot to 90°; gauze support if needed.

cr.angle: 40° cephalad to long axis of foot

collimation: Include entire calcaneus and fifth-metatarsal base; 1 in beyond heel.

views.name: Lateral Mediolateral
key: 1 in distal to medial malleolus.
position: Affected side down; true lateral foot.
IR aligned with plantar heel.
collimation: 1 in beyond heel; include malleolus and fifth-metatarsal base.
evaluation: Tuberosity in profile; open sinus tarsi.

views.name: AP
key: Distal tibiofibular overlap is normal on AP.
position: Supine/seated; leg extended.
Foot upright; ankle in true AP.
collimation: About 8 in lengthwise; 1 in beyond sides; include heel.
evaluation: Normal distal tibiofibular and talofibular overlap.
Medial talomalleolar space open; tibiotalar space shown.

views.name: Lateral
key: Mediolateral; fibula over posterior half of tibia.
position: Affected side down; lateral foot against IR.
Dorsiflex; avoid ankle rotation.
collimation: About 8 in lengthwise; 1 in beyond sides; include heel and fifth-metatarsal base.
evaluation: Talar domes superimposed; tibiotalar joint seen.

views.name: AP Oblique Medial Rotation
key: 45° medial opens distal tibiofibular articulation.
position: Leg extended; foot dorsiflexed.
Rotate entire leg/foot medially 45°.
collimation: About 8 in lengthwise; 1 in beyond sides; include heel.
evaluation: Distal tibia/fibula overlap part of talus.

views.name: Mortise
key: 15–20° medial opens all three mortise sides.
position: Rotate entire leg/foot medially 15–20°.
Intermalleolar plane ∥ IR; foot 90° to leg.

notes: Same CR centering as 45° oblique; rotation and demonstrated joints differ.

collimation: About 8 in lengthwise; 1 in beyond sides; include heel.
evaluation: Anterior tibial tubercle/superolateral talus clear of fibula.

views.name: AP Stress
key: Stress reveals ligament-related joint widening.
position: Maintain AP lower leg; apply prescribed inversion/eversion stress.
Extreme stress positioned/held by physician.
collimation: About 8 in lengthwise; 1 in beyond sides; include heel.
evaluation: Assess widening on injured side under stress.
precautions: Physician controls extreme stress; do not force a painful injured ankle.

views.name: Weight-Bearing AP
key: Both ankles under load; lateral mortise normally closed.
position: Stand with heels against vertical IR.
Toes forward; secure support for balance.

cr.target: Center of IR at ankle level

collimation: About 8 in lengthwise; 1 in beyond sides; include heel.
evaluation: Both ankles centered; medial mortise open.
Distal tibia/talus partly overlap fibula; lateral mortise closed.
precautions: Use a secure platform; never stand a patient on the radiographic table.

views.name: Weight-Bearing Lateral
key: Upright lateromedial option described with lateral ankle.
position: Upright lateral ankle; medial surface against vertical IR.
Patella ⟂ IR; maintain true lateral alignment.

cr.target: ½ in superior to lateral malleolus
notes: Source describes upright use under lateromedial ankle, not a separate weight-bearing protocol.

collimation: About 8 in lengthwise; include heel and fifth-metatarsal base.
evaluation: Fibula over posterior half of tibia.

views.name: AP
key: Both knee and ankle included; use two images if needed.
position: Supine; pelvis straight.
Femoral condyles ∥ IR; foot upright.

notes: 48 in SID can help include more length.

collimation: 1 in beyond sides; 1½ in beyond knee/ankle.
evaluation: Moderate overlap at proximal/distal tibiofibular joints.

views.name: Lateral
key: True lateral leg; joints may need separate images.
position: Affected side down; patella/condylar plane ⟂ IR.
Flex knee/support leg as needed.
collimation: 1 in beyond sides; 1½ in beyond knee/ankle.
evaluation: Slight proximal fibular-head overlap; shafts mostly separated.

views.name: AP
key: CR angle follows ASIS-to-table measurement.
position: Supine; pelvis straight; knee extended.
Femoral epicondyles ∥ IR.

cr.angle: ASIS-to-table: <19 cm → 3–5° caudad; 19–24 cm → ⟂; >24 cm → 3–5° cephalad
cr.target: ½ in inferior to patellar apex

collimation: 8 × 10 in field; about 1 in beyond sides.
evaluation: Slight fibular-head overlap; patella over femur.
Femorotibial spaces open and equal if normal.

views.name: PA
key: 5–7° caudad parallels tibial plateau.
position: Prone; toes down or ankle supported.
Knee extended; epicondyles ∥ IR.

cr.target: Exits ½ in inferior to patellar apex
notes: ⟂ CR may be needed with large thighs or dorsiflexed foot.

collimation: 8 × 10 in field; about 1 in beyond sides.
purpose: PA knee with open joint space.
evaluation: Open, equal femorotibial spaces if normal.

views.name: Lateral
key: 20–30° knee flexion; 5–7° cephalad CR.
position: Affected side down; support ankle.
Epicondyles ⟂ IR; knee flexed 20–30°.
collimation: 8 × 10 in field; about 1 in beyond sides.
evaluation: Patella in profile; open patellofemoral/femorotibial spaces.
precautions: New/unhealed patellar fracture: flex no more than 10°.

views.name: Weight-Bearing AP
key: Extended, equally loaded knees show narrowing.
position: Upright, back to IR; toes forward.
Knees extended; equal weight on feet.
collimation: Include both knees; 1 in beyond sides.
evaluation: Both knees unrotated; joint spaces centered.

views.name: Weight-Bearing PA Rosenberg
key: Standing PA flexion; posterior femoral cartilage assessment.
position: Face IR; knees against it.
Hold support; flex until femora at 45°.

cr.target: Midpopliteal area; exits ½ in below patellar apices

collimation: Include both knees; 1 in beyond sides.
evaluation: Both knees unrotated; tibial plateaus in profile.

views.name: Lateral Oblique
key: 45° lateral rotation → medial condyles.
position: Supine; rotate extremity laterally 45°.

cr.angle: ASIS-to-table: <19 cm → 3–5° caudad; 19–24 cm → ⟂; >24 cm → 3–5° cephalad
cr.target: ½ in inferior to patellar apex

collimation: 8 × 10 in field; about 1 in beyond sides.
evaluation: Fibula over lateral half of tibia.
Patellar margin beyond lateral femoral condyle; open joint.

views.name: Medial Oblique
key: 45° medial rotation → proximal tibiofibular joint.
position: Supine; rotate extremity medially 45°.

cr.angle: ASIS-to-table: <19 cm → 3–5° caudad; 19–24 cm → ⟂; >24 cm → 3–5° cephalad
cr.target: ½ in inferior to patellar apex

collimation: 8 × 10 in field; about 1 in beyond sides.
purpose: Lateral condyles and proximal tibiofibular joint.
evaluation: Patellar margin beyond medial femoral condyle; open joint.

views.name: Holmblad
key: 70° knee flexion from full extension.
position: Supported standing/kneeling variant.
Anterior tibial knee against IR; flex 70°.

cr.target: Superior popliteal fossa; exits at patellar apex

collimation: 8 × 10 in field; 1 in beyond sides.
purpose: Intercondylar fossa and posterior condylar surfaces.
evaluation: Open fossa; patellar apex clear of it.
Knee space open; tibial plateau(s) in profile.

views.name: Camp-Coventry
key: 40° or 50° flexion; matching caudad CR angle.
position: Prone; no rotation.
Support lower leg at 40° or 50°.

cr.target: Popliteal fossa; exits at patellar apex

collimation: 8 × 10 in field; 1 in beyond sides.
evaluation: Open fossa; patellar apex clear of it.
Knee space open; tibial plateau(s) in profile.

views.name: Béclère
key: Supine; femur and tibia axes form 60°.
position: Supine; bend knee until angle between femur/tibia is 60°.
Support knee; condyles equidistant from IR.
collimation: 8 × 10 in field; 1 in beyond sides.
evaluation: Patellar apex clear; slight tibiofibular overlap.

views.name: PA
key: Heel rotated 5–10° laterally → patella ∥ IR.
position: Prone; support painful knee as needed.
Rotate heel laterally 5–10°.
collimation: 6 × 6 in field.
purpose: Patella with reduced OID versus AP.

views.name: Lateral
key: Only 5–10° flexion; CR ⟂, unlike lateral knee.
position: Affected side down; knee flexed 5–10°.
Epicondyles superimposed; patella ⟂ IR.
collimation: 4 × 4 in field at patellofemoral joint.

views.name: Hughston
key: 50–60° knee flexion; 45° cephalad CR.
position: Prone; support lower leg at 50–60°.
No medial/lateral rotation.
collimation: 4 × 4 in field at patellofemoral joint.
evaluation: Patella in profile; femoral condyles/sulcus visible.

views.name: Merchant
key: Relax quadriceps; detailed method uses 40° flexion.
position: Supine; knees supported at table end.
Femora ∥ table; knees flexed 40°.
IR on shins about 1 ft distal; IR ⟂ beam.

notes: Record flexion angle for comparison; source permits other angles for specific disorders.

collimation: 2 in above patellar shadow; 1 in beyond sides.
evaluation: Patella in profile; femoral condyles/sulcus visible.

views.name: Settegast
key: Acute flexion; first exclude transverse patellar fracture.
position: Prone preferred; slowly flex as tolerated.
Aim patella ⟂ IR; no leg rotation.
collimation: 4 × 4 in field at patellofemoral joint.
evaluation: Patella in profile; femoral condyles/sulcus visible.
precautions: Do not attempt before transverse fracture is excluded on lateral image, or if painful.

views.name: AP
key: Proximal view: 10–15° internal rotation per this chapter.
position: Supine; pelvis straight.
Distal: epicondyles ∥ IR; IR 2 in below knee.
Proximal: rotate internally 10–15°; IR top at ASIS.
collimation: 1 in beyond thigh sides; include adjacent joint(s) and entire hardware.
purpose: Femur plus joint nearest concern; image other end as needed.
evaluation: Proximal neck not foreshortened; little/no lesser trochanter.
Distal knee unrotated; entire hardware included.
precautions: Do not force rotation with suspected fracture.

views.name: Lateral
key: Distal and proximal setups differ.
position: Affected side down.
Distal: knee about 45°, epicondyles ⟂ IR.
Proximal: pelvis rolled back 10–15°; other leg moved away.
collimation: 1 in beyond thigh sides; include adjacent joint(s) and entire hardware.
evaluation: Distal: anterior condylar surfaces superimposed, patella in profile.
Proximal: opposite thigh clear; lesser trochanter medial.
precautions: Fracture/destructive disease: remain supine; use horizontal-beam lateral instead.

views.name: AP
key: 15–20° internal leg rotation profiles femoral necks.
position: Supine; ASISs equidistant from table.
Rotate legs internally 15–20° unless contraindicated.

cr.target: Midline, midway between ASIS level and pubic symphysis

collimation: Entire pelvis/proximal femora; about 1 in beyond skin sides.
evaluation: Full femoral necks; greater trochanters in profile.
precautions: No forced internal rotation with trauma/pathologic contraindications.

views.name: Modified Cleaves
key: Bilateral frog-leg; ⟂ CR, not original Cleaves axial.
position: Supine; pelvis unrotated; hips/knees flexed.
Soles together; abduct thighs equally, ideally 45° from vertical.

cr.target: Midline, 1 in superior to pubic symphysis
notes: Unilateral variant: affected foot by opposite knee; CR to femoral neck.

collimation: Entire pelvis/proximal femora; about 1 in beyond skin sides.
purpose: Compare femoral heads, necks and trochanters.
evaluation: Femoral necks not obscured by greater trochanters.
precautions: Contraindicated with suspected fracture or relevant pathologic disease.

views.name: AP
key: 15–20° internal rotation; femoral neck not foreshortened.
position: Supine; pelvis straight.
Internally rotate leg 15–20° unless contraindicated.

cr.target: Femoral neck: 2½ in distal along a perpendicular from midpoint of ASIS–pubic-symphysis line

collimation: 10 × 12 in field; include proximal femur and entire hardware.
purpose: Hip joint and proximal third of femur.
evaluation: Head visible through acetabulum; full neck.
Greater trochanter in profile; little/no lesser trochanter.
precautions: Trauma limb manipulation only under physician direction.

views.name: Lauenstein
key: ⟂ CR; greater trochanter overlaps femoral neck.
position: From supine, rotate slightly toward affected side.
Flex affected thigh near 90° to hip bone; femur ∥ table.
Support opposite limb out of way.

cr.target: Hip joint, midway between ASIS and pubic symphysis

collimation: 10 × 12 in field; include proximal femur and entire hardware.
precautions: Contraindicated with suspected fracture or pathologic condition.

views.name: Hickey
key: 20–25° cephalad frees neck from greater trochanter.
position: From supine, rotate slightly toward affected side.
Flex affected thigh near 90° to hip bone; femur ∥ table.
Support opposite limb out of way.

cr.target: 1 in inferior to Lauenstein centering point

collimation: 10 × 12 in field; include proximal femur and entire hardware.
purpose: Lateral hip with clearer femoral neck.
precautions: Contraindicated with suspected fracture or pathologic condition.

views.name: Danelius-Miller
key: Cross-table lateral; IR ∥ femoral neck.
position: Supine; lift/support unaffected thigh vertically.
Affected leg 15–20° internal only if permitted.
Vertical IR at hip, aligned with femoral neck.

cr.target: Groin through femoral neck, midway between anterior/posterior thigh surfaces

collimation: 10 × 12 in field; include proximal femur and entire hardware.
purpose: Axial lateral hip with minimal affected-limb movement.
evaluation: Unaffected thigh clear of hip; ischial tuberosity below neck.
precautions: Do not manipulate unhealed fracture; physician directs movement.
Do not rest unaffected foot on tube/collimator.

views.name: Judet
key: Two 45° obliques: affected hip up AND down.
position: Internal oblique: affected hip raised 45°.
External oblique: affected hip down; opposite side raised 45°.

cr.target: Hip up: 2 in inferior to affected ASIS. Hip down: pubic symphysis.

collimation: 10 × 12 in field at affected acetabulum.
evaluation: Hip up: anterior (iliopubic) column + posterior rim.
Hip down: posterior (ilioischial) column + anterior rim.

views.name: Taylor Outlet
key: Cephalad beam reduces ramus foreshortening.
position: Supine; pelvis straight; ASISs equidistant.
Slight knee flexion/support for comfort.

cr.target: Midline, 2 in inferior to superior border of pubic symphysis

collimation: 14 × 17 in field; about 1 in beyond skin sides.
evaluation: Rami centered; pubic bones over sacrum/coccyx; hips included.

views.name: Bridgman Inlet
key: 40° caudad shows entire pelvic ring.
position: Supine; ASISs equidistant.
Knees slightly flexed/supported; IR at greater-trochanter level.
collimation: 14 × 17 in field; about 1 in beyond skin sides.
evaluation: Hip joints and anterior pelvic bones included.
